name: Nebuchadnezzar
overview: Nebuchadnezzar was a male king of Babylon, known primarily for his role as a powerful ruler during the period recorded in 2 Kings 23:37. While no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are given, his position as king marks him as a significant figure in biblical history.
namesAndTitles: The name Nebuchadnezzar means 'Nebo protect my boundary stone; Nebo protect my son!' indicating a connection to the Babylonian deity Nebo. His titles include 'King of Babylon,' 'King of the Chaldeans,' 'King of Sheshach,' and 'king of kings,' all reflecting his royal authority over Babylon and surrounding regions. Additionally, Jeremiah refers to him as 'My servant,' a title given by God, highlighting his role in divine purposes despite his pagan kingship.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Nebuchadnezzar as the father of Belshazzar (Daniel 5:1). He is also identified as the king who exiled Jehoiachin (Esther 2:6) and is described as a servant of YHVH in Jeremiah 25:9. Ashpenaz is mentioned in connection with Nebuchadnezzar as his king (Daniel 1:3).
scriptureSignificance: Nebuchadnezzar is a pivotal figure in the biblical narrative as the Babylonian king who executed God's judgment by exiling the people of Judah, including King Jehoiachin. Despite his pagan background, God refers to him as 'My servant,' indicating that Nebuchadnezzar's reign served divine purposes in the unfolding plan of redemption. His rulership over Babylon and the Chaldeans situates him at the center of God's disciplinary actions upon Israel.
